text:
sasha: quick heads-up — the new quantized bring-up (gpt-small-q4) shows pass@5 up ~4 points but exact-match down ~6% vs fp16. odd tradeoff, filing here.
mina: can you paste the eval-run id and config? which seed + tokenizer?
sasha: eval-run id: run-2026-03-20-09-12. config: n_samples=2000, pass_k=[1,5], seed=42, tokenizer=hf/gpt-tokenizer-v2, quant: q4_0.
kevin: I pulled the artifacts. CI job 11802-quant-eval failed once due to timeout but reran. Metrics CSV attached in artifacts. looking like pass@k computed from sampling with replace accidentally? :thinking:
lucas: quick glance: BLEU/ROUGE on the CSV look consistent, but exact-match calc uses whitespace normalization that our tokenizer changed. example: ref="foo  bar" vs pred="foo bar" -> EM false. we used `re.sub(r\\s+"," ", s.strip())` in fp16 path, but quant path skipped it.
anne: also seeing BERTScore diffs — we preprocess refs with `lower()` in one pipeline and not the other. mismatch will change P/R/F1 by a hair but could push EM across threshold.
eval-bot: automated summary: run-2026-03-20-09-12 | pass@1: 0.197 | pass@5: 0.421 | exact_match: 0.604 | bertscore_f1: 0.873 | rouge_l: 0.642 | notes: unusual divergence between pass@k and EM.
ci-bot: rerun queued: quant-eval/11802-rerun (priority: medium). will run with seed sweep [0,42,1337].
sasha: can someone check the pass@k estimator? if sampling used with replacement we overcount duplicates and bias pass@k up.
mina: found a suspicious line in eval-runner sampler: `choices = random.choices(candidates, k=k)` should be `random.sample` for no-replace. that's in `eval_runner/sampler.py` at L87. when candidates < k it currently repeats.
kevin: nice catch. but random.sample was intentionally replaced earlier to let large candidate pools sample faster — for pass@k estimator we must ensure no replacement. propose: use `numpy.random.Generator.choice(..., replace=False)` with the seeded Generator to keep deterministic seeding across workers.
lucas: also for small-n workloads we should prefer exact combinatorial pass@k (enumerate top-k if n<=k_threshold) because the estimator variance is huge. I can add an assert if n<=k_threshold to switch modes.
sasha: good. anne can you open a tiny PR for tokenizer canonicalization? lowercase+NFKC+collapse-whitespace for both branches.
anne: yep. will add unit tests that compare tokenization pipeline outputs and a golden example set. also adding a BERTScore preproc hook to ensure parity.
mina: I'll patch sampler line and add a unit test that simulates candidates=3,k=5 and asserts no-duplicates and deterministic seeds.
kevin: i'll update pass@k docs in repo to include estimator assumptions and add a CI smoke that runs deterministic micro-eval for pass@k, EM and BERTScore on 10 examples.
eval-bot: note: adding tests might add ~20s to unit suite; schedule as fast/flake job first.
ci-bot: new pipeline step: `eval-smoke` added to fast checks (non-blocking).
sasha: plan: (1) fix sampler (mina) (2) canonicalize tokenization + bert preproc (anne) (3) add deterministic pass@k smoke and docs (kevin) (4) add small-n deterministic path (lucas). target: merge by EOD tomorrow, rerun run-2026-03-20 after.
kevin: ack.
mina: on it.
lucas: I'll open an RFC for pass@k small-n exact enumeration later today.
anne: PR incoming in ~2 hours.
sasha: thanks all :thumbsup:
